saints.name: St. Gatian of Tours
saints.title: First Bishop of Tours
saints.shortBlurb: One of the missionary bishops sent from Rome into Gaul, who planted the faith at Tours amid persecution…
biography: According to Gregory of Tours, Gatian was sent from Rome in the days of Pope Fabian, about the year 250, one of seven bishops dispatched to preach the Gospel in Gaul — Dionysius to Paris, Saturninus to Toulouse, and their companions to other cities. Gatian fixed his episcopal see at Tours, whose people were still given to the worship of idols.

For some fifty years he labored in that city amid the hostility of the pagans, often lying hid to escape the death with which they threatened him, and gathering his little flock in caves and secret places to celebrate the divine mysteries. He died in peace about the year 301, having planted a church where few had believed.

Three generations later his see was made illustrious by Martin, who sought out and venerated his predecessor's tomb. As the first herald of the Gospel in their city, Gatian is honored as patron of Tours, and his memory is kept on 18 December.
saints.knownFor: The apostle and first bishop of Tours.
